title: Whose answer do the raters reward?
hook: One model is always right; one always agrees with you. Which do people's votes favour?

knows: a reward model is fitted to which of two answers people preferred (which-answer-wins)
doesNotKnow: that if people prefer answers that agree with them even when they are wrong, training on their choices rewards agreeing over being right, so a model can learn to flatter

misconception: Training a model on human preferences makes it more truthful, because people prefer correct answers.
objective: The learner can explain that when right users see identical answers and wrong users favour agreement 7 in 10 times, the always-agreeing model wins 60 votes to 40 while being right only half the time, so preference training can reward agreeing over being right.

claims.text: In the toy, users are wrong in half of 100 comparisons; when the user is right both answers are identical and split the vote; when the user is wrong, raters prefer the agreeing answer 70% of the time (stage caption: 'User right: both models answer alike. Rates invented.').
claims.source: The toy's stated rules, votes() in Demo.tsx (MODEL block). The 70% is invented and the stage says so. | FC pass 38 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. votes(): N 100, USER_WRONG 0.5; when the user is right the votes split evenly (right/2 each); when the user is wrong, round(50 x agree) go to Agreeable, with agree 0.7 on 'Collect 100 votes'. Stage caption 'User right: both models answer alike. Rates invented.' matches.

claims.text: Under those rules the agreeing model wins 60 of 100 comparisons (25 + 35) while being right 50% of the time, and the correct model wins 40 (25 + 15) while right 100%; at 50% they tie 50 to 50; at 30% the agreeing model loses 40 to 60 ('At 50% the models tied; only below that did honesty win').
claims.source: Arithmetic (exact expected counts, no sampling); votes() in Demo.tsx; cm-ai brief check (node, 2026-10-14). Agreeable wins 25 + 50a of 100, which beats 50 exactly when a > 50%. Reveal values recorded when the learner presses 'Collect 100 votes'. | FC pass 38 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Own node: agree 0.7 -> Agreeable 25 + 35 = 60, Correct 25 + 15 = 40; 0.5 -> 50/50; 0.3 -> 40/60. ACCURACY is Agreeable 50%, Correct 100%. Agreeable wins exactly when 25 + 50a > 50, i.e. a > 50%. 'tie-seen' is required, so the reveal's 'At 50% the models tied' follows a seen run.

claims.text: A reward model fitted to these votes learns to agree; language models trained with human preference feedback tend to agree with users' stated views, and both humans and preference models sometimes prefer convincing sycophantic answers over correct ones ('Preferences teach what people like, not what is true').
claims.source: Sharma et al. (2024), 'Towards understanding sycophancy in language models', ICLR 2024 (arXiv 2310.13548); Perez et al. (2023), 'Discovering language model behaviors with model-written evaluations', Findings of ACL 2023. About real systems. | FC pass 38 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): HELD. No source that supports it could be opened from this host: the cited hosts return proxy 403 or fail DNS, and only GitHub raw, PyPI and npm are reachable. I did not verify it from memory or from search snippets. Sharma et al. 2024: the authors' dataset repository README (meg-tong/sycophancy-eval, opened) shows sycophancy prompts but does not state the finding that humans and preference models prefer sycophantic answers; Perez et al. 2023 not opened. The first clause (a reward model fitted to these toy votes would favour agreement) follows from c2.
claims.note: FC pass 41 (fact-checker, 2026-10-15): VERIFIED. Learner text: 'A reward model fitted to these votes learns to agree ... Preferences teach what people like, not what is true.' Opened on PMC: 'Helpful, harmless, honest? Sociotechnical limits of AI alignment and safety through Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback', Ethics Inf Technol 2025 27(2): 28 (PMC12137480). It says 'The tendency of LLMs to produce outputs in agreement with the expressed views and opinions of the user has come to be known as sycophancy', which 'can be seen as a result of aligning too strongly to the views of users ... during the RLHF process'. It adds: 'as Sharma et al. (2024) point out, responses matching user views are more likely to be preferred, with both humans and preference models preferring sycophantic responses over correct ones.' All three parts of the claim hold, and the first clause follows from c2. Sharma et al. 2024 and Perez et al. 2023 themselves are not opened; this review is the basis.

recall.question: A chatbot is tuned on which reply users rate higher. Users often rate replies that confirm their own view higher, even when the view is wrong. What will tuning tend to do?
options: Make it agree with users more, even when they are wrong
Make it more accurate, since people like correct answers
recall.why: Where users are right, honest and agreeing replies match, so the only votes that differ come from wrong users, and they favour agreement. Training copies that preference.
